title: Four checks before a step-up
objectives: Run the four checks before suggesting any step-up.
Explain why a step-up that squeezes the budget is worse than none.
body_md:
A step-up suits clients whose income is likely to grow, and whose goal is at least 5–7 years away. Check four things before suggesting one.

| Check | Question to ask | Green light | Caution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Income growth | "How much has your income grown each year, on average?" | Salaried with regular raises; growing business | Fixed pension, irregular income |
| Basics | "Is your emergency fund in place? Any high-interest loans?" | 6 months' expenses set aside; no costly debt | No buffer; credit-card or personal-loan debt |
| Budget room | "What share of a raise could go to savings?" | A third to a half of each raise | Raise already committed to EMIs |
| Time left | "When is the goal?" | 7+ years away | Under 3 years (a step-up adds little) |

## Why the basics come first

A step-up that squeezes the budget is the first thing cancelled in a bad month, and cancelling costs more than never having stepped up. The emergency fund is what lets the SIP survive a job change.

## The output of the checks

Either a rate and a date, or a clear reason to wait — and a note recording which.
example: A client with no emergency fund and a personal loan at 14% asks to triple his SIP. The answer is the loan first, the buffer next, and a 5% step-up after that.
say: Before we raise the SIP, let's check that the emergency fund is in place and no costly loans are running.
A step-up you can't sustain is the first thing cancelled in a bad month.
never: You can afford it; let's double the SIP.
The emergency fund can wait until later.

check.q: Name two checks before suggesting a step-up.
o: Income growth and the emergency fund
The fund's star rating and the AMC's AUM
The market level and the tax rate
The number of folios and the nominee
check.why: Income growth, the emergency fund and loans, budget room, and the time to the goal.

check.q: A client has no emergency fund and a 14% personal loan. What comes first?
o: Repay the costly loan and build the buffer before stepping up
A step-up and the loan together
check.why: Basics first: costly debt and a buffer come before a bigger SIP.

check.q: A goal is 2 years away. Does a step-up make sense?
o: No: under 3 years a step-up adds little, and the money may need to move to debt
Yes, but only in a small-cap fund
Only if the market is low
check.why: With under three years to the goal, extra money belongs in debt, not in a larger equity SIP.
